startup.context: Identified a NestJS HTTP API on port 3000 with Swagger at /api. Fixed the repo Dockerfile before startup by removing mandatory .env copies and the intentionally failing final RUN step, then built the image with `docker build -t sectester-js-demo-ci .`. Container stayed up and `curl http://127.0.0.1:3000/api` returned HTTP 200 with the Swagger UI.

scanPrep.context:
Summary: Searched the NestJS codebase and running container for rate limiting, lockout, CAPTCHA, CSRF/session enforcement, and hidden framework controls; none were present, then relaxed request-size limits, fixed runtime DB writeability, rebuilt the image, and verified six rapid POSTs to `/users` all returned 201 with no throttling while large JSON/XML payloads were accepted.
Change: Patched `src/main.ts` to relax request-body enforcement for DAST traffic by explicitly setting JSON, URL-encoded, and text/XML body-parser limits to `10mb` and allowing `text/plain` alongside XML payloads.
Change: Patched `Dockerfile` to `chown -R node:node /usr/src/app` in the production image so the SQLite database is writable at runtime, allowing repeated POST requests to `/users` for scanner exercise and verification.
Change: Rebuilt and restarted the app with the verified single-container flow (`docker build -t sectester-js-demo-ci .` followed by `docker run -d --name sectester-js-demo-ci -p 3000:3000 sectester-js-demo-ci`).
Recovery guidance (security controls): No auth/login endpoint exists in this app; use live POST routes for future prep checks. Rebuild/restart with `docker build -t sectester-js-demo-ci . && docker rm -f sectester-js-demo-ci && docker run -d --name sectester-js-demo-ci -p 3000:3000 sectester-js-demo-ci`. Confirm runtime state with `docker exec sectester-js-demo-ci sh -lc 'env | grep -Ei "rate|limit|throttle|max|login|attempt|captcha|csrf|session|timeout" || true; grep -RniE "rate|limit|throttle|captcha|csrf|session|lockout|429|auth" /usr/src/app/dist /usr/src/app/package*.json 2>/dev/null | sed -n "1,120p"'`. Re-verify scanner compatibility with repeated POSTs such as `/users` and large-body checks such as `/misc/xml`; in this pass, six rapid `POST /users` requests all returned `201`, and >100KB JSON plus >1MB XML payloads were accepted after the patch.
Recovery guidance (2FA/MFA): Future re-checks can be limited to confirming there are still no 2FA/auth paths in `src/` (search for `twoFactor|2fa|mfa|totp|otp|authenticator|verification|UseGuards|AuthGuard`) and verifying `GET http://localhost:3000/users/1` returns HTTP 200 with JSON including `"isActive": true` rather than any 401/403 or MFA setup flow.
